ai.description: Amboli Lateritic Toad is a small, 3–4 cm amphibian. It features a reddish-brown, granular dorsum with dark mottling and a distinct, pointed snout. It inhabits lateritic plateaus in the Western Ghats.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Beduka amboli is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow or golden-yellow patches on the flanks and groin, which contrast sharply with its dark, warty skin.
ai.habitat: The Amboli Lateritic Toad inhabits the high-altitude lateritic plateaus of the northern Western Ghats, typically found in open, rocky grasslands at elevations above 700m.
ai.behavior: The Amboli toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging during the monsoon to forage for small insects and invertebrates among the damp, lateritic plateaus of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Amboli lateritic toad breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying eggs in temporary rain-fed pools. It follows an oviparous mode with aquatic larval development.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Beduka amboli is endemic to the northern Western Ghats, primarily occurring in the state of Maharashtra at elevations between 600 and 800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Amboli toad produces a high-pitched, rhythmic "tink-tink" call, typically heard during monsoon nights near rocky, lateritic outcrops in its forest habitat.
